primary_reason: Nebius reported rapid AI-cloud revenue growth, more than $40 billion of customer commitments, materially expanded contracted-power plans, and strong customer prepayments, but the build-out remains extremely capital intensive and direct point-in-time valuation is not verified in this slow baseline.
strongest_counter_case: Q2 operating cash flow was dominated by customer prepayments while capital expenditures materially exceeded operating cash flow; the company also used equity, pre-funded warrants, convertibles, and secured debt, and it did not disclose a complete quantitative customer-concentration schedule. Execution delays, GPU or power constraints, contract repricing, dilution, or weaker customer prepayments could therefore impair the capacity ramp before it produces durable free cash flow.
invalidation_conditions: Official evidence shows a material cancellation, repricing, delay, or non-renewal of the large contracted AI-cloud commitments.
Verified liquidity, customer prepayments, and financing sources no longer cover the disclosed capacity build-out without materially adverse solvency or dilution risk.
Official evidence shows that GPU availability, power delivery, or data-center construction cannot support the announced capacity ramp.
A validated point-in-time valuation packet shows that expected capacity and cash-flow growth cannot justify the observed enterprise value under conservative assumptions.
next_research_triggers: A validated point-in-time NBIS valuation packet using a completed-session market snapshot and current diluted share count.
The next official earnings release and filed financial statements.
A new official disclosure of customer concentration, contract economics, financing, dilution, GPU supply, power delivery, or data-center commissioning.

claims.normalized_claim: Nebius reported Q2 2026 revenue of $582.3 million, AI-cloud revenue of $574.9 million, more than $40 billion of customer commitments, four landmark deals with an average value above $1 billion, and a target of 5 GW of contracted power by year-end 2026.

For Q2 2026 Nebius reported $2.2461 billion of operating cash flow and $5.6574 billion of capital expenditures; the arithmetic operating-cash-flow-minus-capex proxy is negative $3.4113 billion and is a local calculation rather than a company-reported free-cash-flow metric.

At June 30, 2026 Nebius reported $8.0421 billion of cash and cash equivalents, $1.0560 billion of restricted cash, approximately $8.5 billion of noncurrent debt, and approximately $6.0 billion of current and noncurrent deferred revenue, so headline cash must be assessed together with debt, restrictions, and prepaid delivery obligations.

Nebius disclosed large financing inflows from convertibles, a pre-funded warrant, treasury-share sales and its at-the-market program; during Q2 it sold 12.7 million Class A shares for approximately $2.8 billion gross and retained capacity to sell a further 12.3 million shares under the program.

Large individual contracts, the disclosed Meta framework, a small number of landmark deals, Vera Rubin deployment, power delivery, and data-center construction create material customer and execution concentration; exact customer revenue shares were not disclosed in the reviewed primary sources.

The issuer operating packet is refreshed, but this slow baseline intentionally excludes current market price and does not contain a separately validated point-in-time enterprise-value or diluted-share valuation packet; direct valuation remains unverified.
